subtopics.title: Formulas, Rules & Key Facts
subtopics.subtitle: Drawing conventions, economics, CPM/PERT, earned value, tendering and NEC facts

concepts.text: This chapter is common to every engineering discipline. Its questions mix drawing conventions, a handful of economics and scheduling formulas, and the rules of tendering, contracts, ethics and the Nepal Engineering Council. The tables below collect them in syllabus order. Use this sheet for last-minute revision; each entry is explained with worked examples in its own subtopic.

rows: A0 841 × 1189 mm; each smaller size halves the area (A3 297 × 420, A4 210 × 297)
RF = drawing length / actual length (same units)
top view below the front view
top view above the front view

items: Hatching is a thin line at 45°; full, half, offset, revolved, removed and broken sections suit different shapes.
Shafts, bolts, keys, pins, ribs and spokes are not hatched when cut along their axis.
Oblique views: cavalier keeps receding lengths full size, cabinet halves them; perspective lines converge to vanishing points.

concepts.latex: TF = LS - ES = LF - EF,\qquad FF = ES_{succ} - EF

concepts.plainText: PERT expected time, standard deviation and probability of completion

items: The critical path is the longest path; its activities have zero total float.
Crash the critical activity with the lowest cost slope = (crash cost − normal cost) / (normal time − crash time).
Resource smoothing works within float and keeps the duration; resource levelling respects limits and may extend it.

Tender steps: cost estimate and bid documents → notice → pre-bid meeting → submission with bid security → opening → evaluation → letter of intent → performance security → agreement (Public Procurement Act 2063, Regulations 2064).
Bid security protects the employer if a bidder withdraws; performance security guarantees the winning contractor's performance.
Contract types: lump sum, item-rate (unit-rate), cost-plus (least incentive to control cost), turnkey and EPC.
Dispute resolution: negotiation → mediation → adjudication → arbitration (binding) → litigation.
Risk exposure (EMV) = probability × impact; responses to threats are avoid, transfer (insurance), mitigate and accept.
WACC = equity share × cost of equity + debt share × cost of debt × (1 − tax rate).
Hierarchy of controls: elimination → substitution → engineering controls → administrative controls → PPE.

rows: statutory body under the NEC Act 2055
registers engineers, recognises programmes, disciplines misconduct
professional development, advocacy, code of ethics
Nepal Standards and the NS certification mark

notes.text: Numeric questions here are mostly: scales and RF, compound interest and interest factors, NPV, IRR by interpolation, payback, depreciation, CPM floats and the critical path, PERT expected time and probability, earned value indices and risk exposure. Write the formula before substituting.

Easy swaps: first-angle (top view below) vs third-angle (top view above); bid security vs performance security; NEC (statutory regulator, registration) vs NEA (voluntary professional society); resource smoothing (duration fixed) vs levelling (duration may extend).

Nepal-specific figures such as tax rates, depreciation pool rates, procurement thresholds and fees change through amendments and annual Finance Acts; learn the concepts and confirm figures against the current text.

formulas.title: Compound amount
formulas.description: Future value of a single present sum P after n periods at interest i per period.

formulas.title: Net present value
formulas.description: Discount every cash flow at the MARR; accept the project when NPV is zero or positive.

formulas.title: Straight-line depreciation
formulas.description: P first cost, S salvage value and n useful life; the charge is the same every year.

formulas.title: PERT expected time
formulas.description: a optimistic, m most likely and b pessimistic durations, from the beta distribution.

formulas.title: Performance indices
formulas.description: Values below 1 mean the project is over budget (CPI) or behind schedule (SPI).

flashcards.front: Where is the top view placed in first-angle projection?
flashcards.back: Below the front view (in third-angle projection it is above).

flashcards.front: What is total float and how is it computed?
flashcards.back: The time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project: TF = LS − ES = LF − EF.

flashcards.front: What is the PERT expected time of an activity?
How do NEC and NEA differ?
flashcards.back: NEC is the statutory regulator under the NEC Act 2055 that registers engineers; NEA is the voluntary professional society of engineers.

questions.questionText: Rs 1,000 is invested at a nominal 10% per year compounded continuously. What is its value after 2 years?
questions.explanation: With continuous compounding F = P·e^(rn) = 1,000 × e^0.2 ≈ Rs 1,221.40; annual compounding would give Rs 1,210.

questions.questionText: An activity has ES = 4 and EF = 9 days. Its only successor can start at the earliest on day 12. What is the free float of the activity?
questions.explanation: Free float = ES of the successor − EF of the activity = 12 − 9 = 3 days; the activity can slip 3 days without delaying any successor.

questions.questionText: Which line type is used for centre lines and axes of symmetry in engineering drawings?
questions.explanation: Centre lines use the thin chain line; thick continuous lines show visible outlines, dashed lines hidden edges and wavy lines short break boundaries.

questions.questionText: After receiving the letter of acceptance, the successful bidder must furnish a guarantee that it will carry out the contract as agreed. This guarantee is called the:
questions.explanation: Performance security guarantees the contractor's performance and replaces the bid security, which only protects the employer during the bidding stage.

questions.questionText: A project costs Rs 50,000 and returns Rs 20,000 at the end of every year. Ignoring the time value of money, its payback period is:
questions.explanation: Simple payback = investment / annual inflow = 50,000 / 20,000 = 2.5 years; discounted payback would be longer.
